newsitem.title: USA: Digital, Intel in contact - source.
newsitem.headline: Digital, Intel in contact - source.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp and Intel Corp have had contacts at all levels regarding Digital's patent-infringement lawsuit against Intel, a lawyer close to the negotiations said Friday.
"I know there have been lots of contacts between the companies. There have been all kinds of contacts at all kinds of levels," said the lawyer, who is familiar with Digital's side.

Officials for the two companies declined to comment on a Wall Street Journal report on Friday that said top executives held preliminary discussions recently to try to settle the suit. The talks failed to produce any agreement on a settlement, the Journal said.

The lawyer also declined to say if top executives have discussed a settlement, but he said that Digital was sure of its position and suggested that the company was not under pressure to reach a settlement.
"They wouldn't have filed the case if they didn't think they could win," he said.
People close to Intel's legal defense said they would not be surprised, however, if Digital sought a reconciliation.

Digital's suit, coupled with its sales and marketing troubles, could be hurting its image and turning customers to rivals like Compaq Computer Corp and International Business Machines Corp, they said.
Speculation that Digital is actively pursuing settlement talks would improve its image, a person on Intel's side said.
Digital filed a lawsuit in a Worcester, Mass. federal court in May, accusing Intel of infringement on 10 Digital patents covering key technology for its Pentium family of microprocessors.
Intel is still raking its 1,000 patents on microprocessor design to possibly countersue Digital on patent infringement, Intel lawyers have said.
The lawyer said it was not unusual in patent litigation for two parties to continue to talk to exchange information or to try to hammer out a settlement.
Digital did not seek negotiations before filing the suit, a move that struck some legal observers as odd. But the lawyer said that the move was not so uncommon.
"It's not the case that these are highly unusual circumstances," he said.
